instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Run tool:put-a-picked-option-into-a-filmcraft-project", and give it film, option, project, ops.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:put-a-picked-option-into-a-filmcraft-project and its input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: The result the item's own job names: Put an option I picked for my film into my protected FilmCraft project, and refuse any option I have not picked myself

worked_examples.title: Put the option I picked into my FilmCraft project (runs on your computer) on a sample input

input.film: <film: The film's folder on the person's computer, put where {film} is in the command>
input.option: <option: The option's id, put where {option} is in the command>
input.project: <project: The FilmCraft project file to change, put where {project} is in the command>
input.ops: <ops: The FilmCraft ops file (JSON lines) inside the film's folder, put where {ops} is in the command>

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
